“Repeats” means the point keeps its D1 sign. It is a consistency signal, not good or bad in itself.
This chart came without its rising sign, so only the table is shown.
The main chart describes the overall pattern: identity, life direction, houses, and the natal promise that every other varga must refine rather than replace.
Begin here. No divisional conclusion should contradict a weak or absent promise in D1.
What is the central pattern through which the rest of this reading unfolds?
Planetary signs are comparatively stable; the ascendant and houses still depend on the recorded birth time.
D2 refines the way resources are gathered, protected, shared, and converted into material stability.
Read with the D1 second and eleventh houses, their lords, and Jupiter and Venus strength.
What style of resource-building is easiest to sustain over time?
Use an exact birth time before promoting the D2 ascendant or houses into a firm conclusion.
D4 refines home, property, settlement, emotional rootedness, and the conditions that make a place feel secure.
Read with the D1 fourth house, Moon, Mars, and relevant property or relocation periods.
What conditions help home and long-term security become genuinely restorative?
An exact time is important because the divisional ascendant can change within a short interval.
D7 refines themes of children, caregiving, mentorship, creative continuation, and what is carried into the next generation.
Read with the D1 fifth house, Jupiter, its lord, and supportive timing periods.
How does the chart describe care, continuation, and the legacy you cultivate?
Treat D7 house-based statements as provisional unless the recorded time is exact.
D9 refines relationship maturity, commitments, values, dharma, and how natal potential develops with experience.
Read with the D1 seventh house, Venus, Jupiter, relationship rules, and the active dasha lords.
What qualities help commitment become more mature and sustainable?
D9 is highly useful, but its ascendant should be trusted only when the birth time is exact.
D10 refines vocation, responsibility, leadership, professional visibility, and the way work reaches the wider world.
Read with the D1 tenth house, its lord, Sun, Saturn, Mercury, and current career timing.
Where can competence become visible, useful, and increasingly authoritative?
Small time errors can change the D10 ascendant; confirm it before making specific career claims.
D12 refines parental influence, ancestry, inherited habits, and the family patterns a person carries forward or consciously changes.
Read with the D1 fourth and ninth houses, Sun, Moon, and family-domain evidence.
Which inherited patterns provide support, and which are ready to be handled differently?
Use exact-time data for the D12 ascendant and house emphasis.
D24 refines education, learning style, disciplined study, teachers, and how knowledge becomes usable mastery.
Read with the D1 fourth, fifth, and ninth houses, plus Mercury and Jupiter strength.
Which conditions make learning deeper, more consistent, and easier to apply?
At this resolution, exact birth time and boundary awareness are essential.
D30 refines how strain, conflict, vulnerability, and recovery are experienced. It is best used for practical risk awareness, not fear-based prediction.
Read with the D1 sixth, eighth, and twelfth houses, Saturn and Mars, and measured support factors.
What helps you respond to pressure without letting it define the whole story?
High sensitivity makes exact-time input necessary for house-level interpretation.
D60 is a very fine-grained traditional layer used to qualify deeper patterning. It should never be treated as a standalone verdict or used to override more stable evidence.
Use only after D1, the relevant domain varga, strength measures, and timing all point in the same direction.
Does this fine layer repeat an already well-supported theme, or merely introduce noise?
D60 needs a rectified or exceptionally precise birth time; otherwise treat it as exploratory only.
A short guide to the app and the words it uses.
Your chart, the period of life you are in, and what the chart points to first. Start here.
The periods running now, the week ahead, today’s transits, good times for a task, and this year’s chart.
Photograph a palm and read its lines, two readings a week.
The charts saved on this phone, your preferences, and this Help.
At the foot of the Reading tab: life areas, questions for the classics, and every divisional chart.
A map of where the planets stood at your birth date, time and place. Every reading here starts from it.
The sign rising on the eastern horizon as you were born. It sets where the houses begin, which is why the birth time matters.
One of twelve divisions of the chart, each tied to a part of life such as work or partnership.
One of 27 star divisions of the zodiac. The one your Moon was in at birth sets the order of your dashas.
A planetary period, used to read how themes unfold over time. Smaller periods, antar and pratyantar, sit inside the larger ones.
A combination of planets the tradition gives a particular meaning. What it means depends on the rest of the chart; it is not a promise of an outcome.
A chart drawn from the same birth positions by dividing each sign, to look closely at one theme: D9 for partnership, D10 for work. The finer ones need an exact birth time.

The ayanamsha sets where the zodiac starts, and the house system how the sky is cut into houses. Lahiri with whole-sign houses is the default; another choice can move a point that sits near a boundary.
Planetary positions are calculated; the readings interpret them within astrology. They describe possible themes, not certain events.
With an approximate birth time, the rising sign, houses and timing can shift. Treat those parts as a first look.
